ip_top_stories.title: Taylor and Francis Journal Finder: How It Works
ip_top_stories.summary: Taylor & Francis has published details on how its Journal Finder tool operates, offering guidance for researchers on matching manuscripts to appropriate journals within the publisher's portfolio. The tool is part of the publisher's broader suite of author services.

ip_top_stories.title: Thomson Reuters v. ROSS: Using Copyrighted Works In AI Training Is Not Fair Use
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has ruled in Thomson Reuters v. ROSS Intelligence that using copyrighted legal content to train an AI system does not qualify as fair use, marking a significant decision in AI copyright law. The ruling has broad implications for AI developers who rely on third-party content for model training.

ip_top_stories.title: Democratic lawmakers probe DOJ filing in OpenAI copyright case
ip_top_stories.summary: Democratic members of Congress are investigating a Department of Justice filing in an ongoing copyright case involving OpenAI, raising questions about the administration's position on AI and intellectual property. The probe reflects growing legislative scrutiny over how the DOJ is engaging with AI copyright litigation.

ip_top_stories.title: DistroKid Hands Over AI Music Data in Suno Copyright Lawsuit
ip_top_stories.summary: Music distributor DistroKid has produced AI-detection documents in the Suno copyright lawsuit brought by UMG and Sony, after a subpoena motion was subsequently withdrawn by the record labels. The case centres on whether Suno's AI music generation system infringed copyrighted recordings used in training.

ip_top_stories.title: Australian music industry rejects 'divide and conquer' proposal to give musicians exemption from AI scraping
ip_top_stories.summary: Australia's music industry has rejected a government proposal that would have granted musicians a specific exemption from AI data scraping, warning that such a carve-out would undermine broader creator protections. Creatives and industry groups have criticised the approach as pitting different creative sectors against each other.

ip_further_links.title: Literary Translators Warn AI Threatens Their Livelihoods in Copyright Case
ip_further_links.summary: Literary translators have filed submissions in a copyright case warning that AI tools trained on translated works threaten their professional livelihoods and the legal protections afforded to their creative output.

ip_further_links.title: In landmark AI copyright settlement, this Keene author's getting a cut
ip_further_links.summary: A New Hampshire author is set to receive compensation as part of a landmark AI copyright settlement, one of the first cases in which individual creators have secured direct financial redress from an AI company.

ip_further_links.title: Amicus Urges Compensation and Authorization in AI Use Affecting Creators
ip_further_links.summary: An amicus brief has been filed urging courts to require both compensation and prior authorisation when AI systems make use of creative works, in a case with significant implications for creator rights.

ip_further_links.title: South Africa secures publisher revenue and AI content protections in X and X.AI settlement
ip_further_links.summary: South African publishers have reached a settlement with X and X.AI that includes protections for publisher content used in AI training and provisions for revenue sharing.

ip_further_links.title: Congress Faces Decisions on AI Training and Copyright Law
ip_further_links.summary: US lawmakers are facing mounting pressure to clarify how existing copyright law applies to AI training data, with multiple competing legislative proposals under consideration.

ip_further_links.title: AI Is Changing the Book Business. The Literary Community Is Pushing Back
ip_further_links.summary: Authors, agents, and publishers are organising opposition to AI tools that use copyrighted literary works without authorisation, as the book industry grapples with the commercial and legal implications of generative AI.

ip_further_links.title: Elton John backs Australian artists in fight against AI in surprise Aria awards appearance
ip_further_links.summary: Elton John made a surprise appearance at the Aria Awards to voice support for Australian artists campaigning against AI systems that scrape and reproduce creative works without consent or compensation.

ip_further_links.title: Canada weighed Meta exemption from Online News Act; publishers warn against weakening law
ip_further_links.summary: Canadian publishers have warned against any moves to weaken the Online News Act after reports that the government considered granting Meta an exemption from its provisions requiring platforms to compensate news publishers.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — Building a Taxonomy of Bots
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen publishes a guest post proposing a structured taxonomy for classifying web crawlers and bots, with implications for how publishers assess and respond to AI scraping activity.

ip_further_links.title: AI Copyright Decisions Raise Broader Questions About Institutional Governance
ip_further_links.summary: Recent AI copyright rulings are prompting debate about whether courts and legislatures are the appropriate institutions to resolve fundamental questions about how AI interacts with intellectual property law.
